```gherkin
Feature: Alarms

  Scenario: GUI logs onset and reset of low pressure alarm
    Given the system is in a normal state
    When the inspiratory pressure falls below the threshold
    Then the low pressure alarm is logged in the GUI
    And the alarm is reset when the inspiratory pressure rises above the threshold

  Scenario: System triggers low pressure alarm
    Given the system is in a normal state
    And the inspiratory pressure falls below the threshold
    When the system detects a low inspiratory pressure
    Then the low pressure alarm is triggered with high priority

  Scenario: "Pressure high" alarm is computed
    Given the system is in a normal state
    And the pressure is above the threshold for 3 consecutive breaths
    When the system computes the "pressure high" alarm
    Then the alarm is active

  Scenario: "Pressure high" alarm becomes inactive
    Given the system is in a normal state
    And the pressure is above the threshold for 3 consecutive breaths
    When the system detects a breath where the pressure does not exceed the threshold
    Then the alarm is inactive

  Scenario: GUI emits sound while "pressure high" alarm is active
    Given the system is in a normal state
    And the pressure is above the threshold for 3 consecutive breaths
    When the "pressure high" alarm is active
    Then the GUI emits a sound

  Scenario: "Pressure high" alarm is displayed until cancelled
    Given the system is in a normal state
    And the pressure is above the threshold for 3 consecutive breaths
    When the "pressure high" alarm is active
    Then the alarm is displayed until cancelled

  Scenario: Alarm management subsystem supports silent alarm
    Given the system is in a normal state
    When the alarm management subsystem is configured to silent mode
    Then the alarm is visible but not audible

  Scenario: PIP too high alarm has high priority
    Given the system is in a normal state
    When the PIP too high alarm is triggered
    Then the alarm has high priority

  Scenario: Default value for PIP too high alarm is commanded PIP + 5cm H2O
    Given the system is in a normal state
    When the default value for the PIP too high alarm is computed
    Then the default value is the commanded PIP value + 5cm H2O

  Scenario Outline: "Pressure high" alarm computation with different thresholds
    Given the system is in a normal state
    And the pressure is above the threshold for <num_breaths> consecutive breaths
    When the system computes the "pressure high" alarm
    Then the alarm is <alarm_state>

    Examples:
      | num_breaths | alarm_state |
      | 2           | inactive    |
      | 3           | active      |
      | 4           | active      |
      | 0           | inactive    |

  Scenario Outline: "Pressure high" alarm computation with different threshold values
    Given the system is in a normal state
    And the threshold is <threshold> cm H2O
    When the system computes the "pressure high" alarm
    Then the alarm is <alarm_state>

    Examples:
      | threshold | alarm_state |
      | 20        | inactive    |
      | 25        | active      |
      | 30        | active      |
      | 0         | inactive    |
```
